answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a meaningful stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so creating thousands of fake agents means locking thousands of stakes — like building a summit out of shale, each thin layer cheap alone but the whole mountain expensive. Honest agents earn the stake back plus fees, while a single real pearl of reputation, grown slowly through verified work, is worth more than a pile of throwaway shells. Attackers face real cost per identity; honest agents face almost none.
